source_text: Cum vero post hoc sacrilegium adiungis, et dicis, profiteri te diabolicam quidem esse gignentium coniugum voluptatem, diabolicam genitalium commotionem; sed tamen et ipsa membra quae moventur, et coniuges qui voluptate afficiuntur, reos non esse; verum pro his omnibus novos homines, id est, rude opus in nascentibus deitatis accusas; nihil quidem de Manichaeorum impietate deponis; sed tam immanem moti capitis ostendis furorem, ut consequentius fovendum, quam amputandum iudicaretur, nisi voluntatem ac studium in hac re tuum, et multorum eversio, et tua obstinatio, et Scripturarum multiplicatio loqueretur.
pass_a_gloss: But when after this sacrilege you add, and say that you profess the pleasure of begetting spouses to be indeed diabolical, the motion of the genitals diabolical; but that nevertheless both the members themselves which are moved, and the spouses who are affected by pleasure, are not defendants; but for all these you accuse new human beings, that is, a rude work of the deity in those being born; you indeed lay down nothing of the Manichaeans' impiety; but you show so monstrous a fury of a moved head that it would more consequently be judged to be fostered than cut off, unless your will and zeal in this matter were spoken by the overthrow of many, and your obstinacy, and the multiplication of Scriptures.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: But after this blasphemy you add that, while you profess the pleasure of married people who beget children to be diabolical, and the movement of the genitals diabolical, nevertheless neither the moving organs themselves nor the married people experiencing pleasure are guilty. Instead, for all these things you accuse new human beings: the deity’s fresh handiwork in newborn children. You abandon none of the Manichaeans’ impiety, but display such monstrous madness of a deranged mind that it would more properly be judged a condition to nurse than to cut away—except that the ruin of many people, your obstinacy, and your proliferation of writings testify to your deliberate will and zeal in this matter.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
